description: Dataset name. Most studies have one dataset; a few have two.
Experiment within the dataset, usually one design or one source file. Labels follow the authors' files, not always the paper's experiment numbers.
Study name: first author, year and journal of the paper.
One sequence of trials from one participant, coded within this dataset.
One participant, coded within this dataset. A person can have more than one sequence, for example two runs.
Kind of identifier the authors used for participants. The identifiers themselves are not included.
How sure it is that one person code is one human: verified (platform identifier or documented link), assumed_unique, or unknown (the same human may appear under more than one code).
Between-participant condition, in the authors' naming. Empty for single-group experiments.
true if the participant had done an earlier perturbation experiment, including another study in OpenMotor; false if the paper excluded such participants; otherwise unknown.
The original analysis excluded this whole sequence.
Why the authors excluded the sequence. Empty unless excluded.
The paper's learner classification, for papers that make one. Empty otherwise.
Age in years.
Sex or gender as reported.
Handedness.
Visual acuity.
Medication state at testing, for clinical groups.

values_or_units: mouse, trackpad, touchscreen, tablet, robot, kinarm, other, mouse_or_trackpad, unknown
description: Input device. tablet means a digitizing tablet; mouse_or_trackpad when the paper does not say which.
Tested online or in the lab.

values_or_units: healthy, parkinsons, cerebellar_degeneration, low_vision, deafferented, unknown
description: Sample population. Healthy older adults count as healthy.
Trial number within the sequence, from 0, counting every trial in order across sessions, including practice, no-feedback, probe and placeholder trials.
The authors' own trial number. It may restart at a new session, and is empty when the authors' files are ordered by position only.
Visit number within the sequence, from 0.
The authors' block label.

values_or_units: practice, baseline, learning, aftereffect, washout, relearning, probe, transfer, other
description: Standardized phase of the block.

values_or_units: reach, proprio_probe, aim_report_only, other, demo, missing
description: reach; proprio_probe (the hand was moved passively, no reach); aim_report_only; demo (an instructed demonstration reach); missing (a placeholder row for a gap in the authors' trial numbers, with no data); other.
A documented pause came before this trial: the first trial, a new session, a rest break or an instruction screen.
Target onset time since the first trial of the sequence.
Time from the end of the previous trial to this trial's target onset.
Direction of the target, the instructed goal of the movement. 0 points right and angles increase counter-clockwise.
Target location within the experiment, one per direction and distance.
Direction of the displayed stimulus when it differs from the goal, for example when people reach opposite the stimulus.
Angular radius of the target at the target distance.
Target distance divided by the largest target distance in the experiment.
False if the target disappeared when the movement started.
Display size relative to the experiment's reference display (1 = reference).
What the target did after movement onset.
How far the target jumped after movement onset; 0 for none and flicker.
Time of the target event after movement onset.
Proprioceptive probe: active_post_reach (felt hand reported after the participant's own reach), or passive_robot and passive_experimenter (the hand was moved for them).
On passive probes, where the hand was moved to.
What participants were told to bring to the target: the cursor, the hand, or the hand at an instructed angle.
Instructed hand direction relative to the target, when instr_goal is hand_to_angle.

values_or_units: allowed, forbidden, maintain, remove, given_with_angle, unspecified
description: Instruction about aiming: allowed; forbidden (for example, ignore the cursor); maintain; remove (stop aiming and reach straight to the target); given_with_angle (told where to aim); unspecified.
Instructed aiming direction relative to the target, when instr_strategy is given_with_angle.
What participants were told about the perturbation: nothing, that there is one, or exactly what it is.
Report collected on the trial: an aim report, the felt hand position after a reach, or after a passive movement.
Whether the aim report came before or after the reach.
Contextual cues present before the movement, joined with | (for example light|tone or target_color:red).
Time from cue onset to the go signal.
Lower bound of a forced preparation-time window.
Upper bound of a forced preparation-time window.
Time from target onset to the go signal.
Participants knew before moving whether a cursor would be shown, from a blocked design or an explicit cue.
Hand that moved, or that was moved on passive probes.
Direction of the hand relative to the target, counter-clockwise positive, from the earliest reliable measure the authors recorded (see hand_measure).
Hand direction that determined the cursor, for example the endpoint at the target distance.
How hand_angle was measured. Constant within an experiment.
Movement extent in units of the target distance.
Reaction time.
Movement time.
Reported aiming direction relative to the target.
Reported felt hand position relative to the target. On passive probes, the proprioceptive error.
The original analysis excluded this trial. Also true on placeholder rows.
What was shown: no cursor, a cursor during the movement, or the cursor only at or after the end of the movement (including delayed feedback).

values_or_units: none, veridical, rotated, clamped, mirror, gain, other, unknown
description: How the cursor related to the hand.
Form of the feedback.
What the cursor did during the movement.
A veridical cursor during the movement was followed by a transformed endpoint.
Visuomotor rotation in force: cursor = hand_angle_fb + rotation. 0 on veridical trials.
Cursor direction relative to the target on error-clamp trials, 0 degree clamps included.
Mirror axis on mirror trials.
Extent gain on gain trials: cursor extent = gain x hand extent.
Endpoint shift dx,dy in units of the target distance, on other-mapping trials.
Spread of a cloud or blurred cursor at the target distance.
Number of cursors, when more than one was shown.
Where the cursor ended up relative to the original target, as the participant saw it. Empty when no cursor was shown.
Cursor extent minus the target distance, in target-distance units.
Delay of the feedback after the end of the movement; 0 if immediate.
How long the feedback stayed on screen.
Outcome signals shown on the trial, joined with | (cursor, hit_color, points, reward_tone, symbolic_error).
Reward delivered on the trial. Empty if the task had none.
Number shown to the participant: points, or a signed error.
Maximum possible score.
Whether the reward rule was applied to the cursor or to the hand.
Center of the rewarded zone relative to the target.
Half-width of the rewarded zone.
The cursor hit the target.
A too-slow or too-fast message was shown.
Another warning was shown, for example too far.
